description: §23.5.5 — the presence-nudge lint fires for a `_{}` INLINE foreign-code block (§23.2), not just the `use foreign:` sidecar the existing cases exercise. An inline value-returning `_={ … }=` block sits inside a `<program lang="ts">` with NO `capabilities=` on any ancestor → governed by the empty set → W-FOREIGN-UNDECLARED-CAPABILITY (Info). Unlike the sidecar cases, the inline `_{}` form does NOT co-fire the sidecar-runtime Nominal error (S356 r4: `E-NESTED-PROGRAM-CONTEXT-NOMINAL`, at the nested-`<program>` declaration; before that, the now-RETIRED `E-FOREIGN-SIDECAR-NOMINAL` at the `use foreign:` site) — an inline `_{}` block declares no nested `<program>` and makes no `use foreign:` reference, so neither the declaration-site refusal nor §23.4's `E-FOREIGN-010` has anything to fire on. That is what makes this the cleanest single-construct proof of the lint. Twin of `inline-block-covered`. NOTE: this case NAMES those codes in prose only; the `expect` block below pins nothing about them, so nothing here would catch a regression in the sidecar codes.
rationale: §23.5.5: the compiler SHALL emit W-FOREIGN-UNDECLARED-CAPABILITY (Info) when a foreign-code construct — a `_{}` block (§23.2), WASM sigil (§23.3), or `use foreign:` sidecar (§23.4) — is governed by an empty capability set. Here the `_={ … }=` block has no ancestor `capabilities=`, so the empty-set nudge fires. §23.5.5 opacity bound: it checks declaration-PRESENCE only. No E-SCOPE-001, no E-FOREIGN-CAPABILITY-UNKNOWN.
